sheets.noticed: A hand-drawn trail map on lined paper, with a bold title. It looks handmade and pleasant. Still in.
A red line draws up the trail from the trailhead, and the blue '2.1 km to the creek' label fills in. The line moving is a good hook. Still in.
The creek crossing gets a 'cross on the stones' note. The caption overlaps a map label a little, but it is still readable. Still in.
The red line keeps going and the ridge junction starts to show up. The frames look much the same, but the route is moving. Still in.
A red circle marks the ridge junction at 4 km, and the route is now drawn up to it. A clear visual beat. Still in.
'Here's where people go wrong' with a red X on the right fork. The warning is a real hook. Still in.
A blue arrow for 'keep left' and the wrong fork gets crossed out. Clear, and the map is getting busy. Still in.
'Right fork: back to the road' is in red, and the map carries all the marks. Busy but readable. Still in.
Mostly static now, the same marked map with 'drops back down' and 'to the road'. Thinning out, still in for the reveal.
The X marks clear and the map resets to show keep left. The un-draw is nice, but I am tiring of the same frame. Still in, barely.
The red route pushes up toward the summit. The line moving is the most interesting thing so far. Still in.
The map has sat almost unchanged for several sheets, and the 5.6 km summit detail is just text. I would thumb past it here.
Not watched; swiped away at sheet 12.

remembers: From the trailhead it's about two kilometers to the creek; cross on the stones, then climb to the ridge junction at four kilometers. People go wrong there, so keep left, not the right fork that drops back to the road. The summit is a kilometer and a half past the junction, at 5.6 km.
